title: Ukraine hits Crimean bridge for third time this week, halting rail link as Putin meets Trump
dek: Russia says no one was hurt in the overnight drone attack, days after a road span fell into the Kerch Strait; the damage has not been independently verified.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ukraine struck Russia's bridge to occupied Crimea for the third time this week overnight into Thursday, halting the rail traffic that had kept running across the crossing since Tuesday's attack sent a road span into the Kerch Strait. Russia's transport ministry said train services had been temporarily suspended because of a Ukrainian drone attack, that "there were no casualties as a result of the incident" and that specialists would assess the damage.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, said on Telegram that the bridge had been hit just after midnight local time and that traffic had been stopped while damage was assessed, according to reports. The attack came hours before Russian President Vladimir Putin met US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, where Trump said he hoped "something will come out" on ending the war, and before Putin's first three-way meeting with Trump and China's Xi Jinping.

## Thursday's attack

Neither side had given details of the damage by Thursday afternoon, and the extent of it could not be independently verified. Rail traffic had been the bridge's only remaining link since Tuesday: Ukraine's General Staff said after that attack that the roadway was out of action and that the railway section was still standing but with a damaged arch, according to reports. Ukrainian analysts have said in interviews that repairs to the road section could take a year or more.

Russia also launched strikes across Ukraine as Putin and Trump met, reports said. A Russian drone attack on Kyiv on Wednesday injured three people and hit a 28-storey residential building, according to reports.

## Tuesday's strike

A section of the road bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea lay in the Kerch Strait on Tuesday after a second Ukrainian attack on the 19 km crossing in two days. Ukraine's security service, the SBU, said "one of the metal arches and the automobile span under it were completely destroyed", and that the railway section had also been damaged. Russia's transport ministry said road and rail traffic had been suspended and that, according to preliminary information, no one had been killed on the bridge. By the afternoon, Crimea's Russian-installed head said rail services had resumed and foot passengers could cross by ferry.

The strike came on the same night that Russian ballistic missiles hit two road bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv, cutting heating and water to parts of the capital, and two days before Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, where ending the war is expected to be on the agenda. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the bridge strike was a response to Russia's attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure.

Zelensky described the attack as the "seventh phase of an operation that has been underway for several weeks", during which, he said, Ukrainian forces had "systematically destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare assets" around the crossing, according to reports. He said Palianytsia drones had struck the road section, while Neptune missiles and Ruta and FP-5 drones were used against the railway section; a Flamingo missile was also used, reports said. Footage he published showed the main road arch and part of the roadway missing between two supports. "Today, parts of it lie on the seabed," the SBU said. None of the Ukrainian claims about weapons or earlier phases can be independently verified.

The attack followed a first strike on the bridge overnight into Monday, when Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down a record 1,336 Ukrainian drones. Russia's defence ministry said on Tuesday that its air defences had destroyed more than 1,400 drones over 23 regions in the latest overnight attack; the figures cannot be independently verified.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, wrote on Telegram at 11.06 am IST that "the enemy again attacked the Crimean bridge", that traffic had been suspended, and asked residents and visitors not to travel towards the crossing. In a separate post he said two people had been killed by a Ukrainian drone attack in Crimea's Leninsky district. At 3.48 pm IST he said rail services between Crimea and Taman, on the Russian side of the strait, had resumed and that passengers without vehicles could use the ferry crossing; he made no mention of when road traffic would resume. Authorities in Russia's Krasnodar region said food and warming points had been set up on the approaches to the bridge for stranded drivers.

In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian missiles had hit the Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro, damaging heating mains and leaving hundreds of apartment buildings without heat, reports said. Russia's defence ministry said its strikes were aimed at military production and at transport, energy and port infrastructure.

## What Russia says

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Tuesday: "There is no doubt that the bridge will be restored." He said Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, who chairs a government commission on the bridge, had briefed Putin. Russian investigators opened a case into what they called a "terrorist attack", reports said.

Ukraine's presidential sanctions envoy, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, posted a picture of the damaged span with the words "Crimean Bridge. Sanctioned." Russia has given no estimate of how long repairs will take.

## Background

Russia built the bridge after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, a move the UN General Assembly declared invalid in a 2014 resolution, and opened the road section in 2018 and the railway in 2019. It is the only fixed road and rail link between Russia and the peninsula and carries fuel, goods and military supplies as well as passengers. Russia also supplies Crimea by ferry and over land through the parts of southern Ukraine it occupies.

The bridge was badly damaged twice before, in October 2022, when a truck exploded on it, and in July 2023, in an attack Ukraine later said it had carried out with sea drones. Neither attack put the crossing out of action for long, according to reports.

The attacks come as US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates last week ended without a breakthrough, and as Ukraine has stepped up long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries, depots and petrochemical plants this month. Zelensky had said before the Shenzhen meeting that Ukraine would keep striking Russia. The Kremlin has said the next round of Russia-Ukraine talks should involve only the US, Russia and Ukraine, without European governments.

## Why it matters for India

India has not taken sides in the war and has called for dialogue. Prime Minister Narendra Modi told the East Asia Summit in Manila on Tuesday that "whether in Ukraine or West Asia, we will continue to support every effort for peace". India remains one of the largest buyers of Russian crude, and an escalation in strikes on energy and transport infrastructure on both sides affects oil and fuel markets that India depends on.

## What happens next

Russia's government commission is expected to set out plans for repairing the bridge; with both road and rail traffic halted, passengers depend on the ferry, and freight on the land route through occupied southern Ukraine. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to hold their three-way talks in Shenzhen later on Thursday; neither Ukraine nor any European government will be at the table. The Declaration will update this story as Russia and Ukraine give fuller accounts of the damage.

## Key numbers

- 19 km: length of the Kerch Strait bridge, Russia's only fixed link to Crimea
- 1,400+: Ukrainian drones Russia says it destroyed overnight into Tuesday, over 23 regions
- 3: Ukrainian attacks on the bridge since Monday
- 19 November: Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen
